observed_original_abi.calling_convention_observation: 0x00c37120 is FLD dword ptr [ECX + 0x768] / RET. ECX is read and nothing else is read from any register; there is no stack argument read ([ESP+0x4] and above never appear) and the RET is bare, so the callee pops zero words. That combination is only produced by a receiver in ECX with no stack arguments. Every one of the 15 xref sites pushes no argument before the CALL, which corroborates the no-stack-argument half but cannot by itself distinguish __thiscall from a cdecl function that happens to take its pointer on the stack - the ECX read is what fixes it.

semantic_contract: Return the 32-bit IEEE-754 single stored at receiver+0x768, widened onto the x87 stack in ST(0). The function is total on its receiver and total on its input: there is no branch, no callee, no global read and no null check, so a null receiver faults inside the FLD and every non-null receiver yields the same four bytes it holds. The result is a copy, not a reference: the field is read once and never written back. The observable contract is therefore exactly 'read one float out of the receiver at a fixed offset', with no state, no lifecycle and no ownership effect.
classification_rationale: Every instruction, the frame, the field offset, the return mechanism and the return width are read directly from the live disassembly and the live bytes, and seven callsite windows independently confirm the float-in-ST(0) return. It is not STRONG_SEMANTIC because two material elements stay bounded rather than established: the owning class of the receiver is not identified anywhere in the binary (0x00dc0230 even passes a sub-object at +0x68c, so the receiver type is not the same as the caller's this type), and the domain meaning of the +0x768 float is not determined by any inspected caller. It is not STRUCTURAL_ONLY because a real behavioural claim is supported beyond layout: the return is a widened copy of a specific field, and the polarity of 'no work, no side effect' is established.
semantic_findings: The whole contract is a single 4-byte load. Everything else about the function is absence: no frame, no callee, no global, no branch, no write.
The 7-byte body and the bare RET are identical under __thiscall, __cdecl and __fastcall except for where the pointer arrives, and the body reads ECX, so ECX is where it arrives.

All 15 xref sites use the same 5-byte E8 rel32 CALL form and none of the seven inspected windows touches a GPR after the call: the result is only ever used on the x87 stack. That is consistent with a compiler-generated float accessor and rules out a float-to-int or float-to-pointer reinterpretation at any inspected site.

0x0101d130 calls the function twice in one body (0x0101d166 and 0x0101d1a0) and subtracts the first result from the second at 0x0101d1ae, which means the field is a live quantity that changes within a frame, not a compile-time constant folded into the accessor.
0x00dc0230 passes [ESI + 0x68c] as the receiver, so the receiver of this method is a sub-object of some other object in at least one call site. Any owning-class claim has to accommodate that.
unresolved_questions: Which class owns the +0x768 float, and is the receiver in every call site the same type? 0x00dc0230 disproves the naive 'the receiver is the caller's this' assumption, and no vtable was located for the receiver in any caller.

What does the float represent? The sibling at 0x00c370e0 compares a float from a +0x34 sub-object against the constant 0x0146bb74 with COMISS, so the object participates in float comparisons, but nothing observed names the quantity.

Is the field written by any function in the binary? No writer of +0x768 was located, so the value's provenance is unestablished; it is only read here and, as far as this batch saw, at the other 14 sites.
Why does the brief's canonical record list 12 callers while Ghidra reports 15 xref sites, and who owns the 0x0101715e callsite? Ghidra attributes no function to that address.

Is 0x00c37120 reachable through a vtable slot anywhere? All 15 xrefs are direct CALLs; no dword equal to 0x00c37120 was searched for in this batch, so the accessor may also be a virtual method whose slot was not found.
runtime_gates: No original-process trace has been captured for 0x00c37120. A differential test must confirm that the shipping build still loads the float from +0x768 and that no runtime patch retargets the address.
The domain of the returned float can only be established by observing one call site in the original process with a known receiver, which no recorded run has done.
